transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-30 14:00 PT
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Aisha Rahman (Tritonix Head of ML), Dan Cooper (CTO), Marta Silva (Infra), Tyrell Gomez (Finance)

--- OPTIONAL AUTO SUMMARY (auto gen, may be noisy)
Quick notes: costs up 18% month over month, burst events are main driver, considering Dedicated reserve for peak 2x events, concern about audit logs retention and KMS key rotation.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll do a quick QBR style check in, go over governance questions, the burn rate, and then line up the roadmap items and the pilot success criteria. Aisha, Dan, you good to go?
[00:08] Aisha Rahman: Yeah thanks Sophie, appreciate it. We've got Marta and Tyrell on as well. We wanted to make sure this call goes through the security stuff early, because legal is watching the SOC doc and the SSO flows.
[00:17] Dan Cooper: And I'll be listening for cost controls; we ran into an unexpected spike last month that ate into our margin.
[00:22] Sophie Chen: Got it. Quick agenda, we'll do 10 minutes usage/costs, 15 minutes governance, 20 minutes perf and dedicated sizing, then wrap with action items. Sound ok?
[00:31] Dan Cooper: Yep.
[00:33] [00:45] Ravi Patel: (SE) Quick caveat — some of the numbers you saw in the dashboard use estimated tokenization for a few pipelines; there may be a small mismatch vs what your internal meter shows. We're tracking that discrepancy.
[00:56] Marta Silva: That's fine, as long as it's within 5%. The spike on July 12th was the killer, where a downstream job retried 12 times.
[01:06] Sophie Chen: We flagged that event in the incident timeline. Looks like a retry loop in your orchestration. Two immediate levers we discussed: short-term throttle + host fallback; medium-term is Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable headroom.
[01:20] Tyrell Gomez: Can you remind me, Sophie, how Dedicated billing works again? We prefer committed monthly vs pure usage because finance hates surprises.
[01:26] Sophie Chen: Sure — Dedicated is reserved GPU pools. You pick a monthly commitment, which buys you guaranteed throughput and lower per-token unit economics. There's also burst credits depending on the plan. If you want pure pay-as-you-go we can keep you on hosted, but costs for sustained peaks will be higher.
[01:40] [02:00] Aisha Rahman: From an ML perspective we want to keep latency tight for interactive clinician flows. If latency goes >200 ms tail we see a drop in task completion. How do you ensure 99th percentile latency?
[02:12] Ravi Patel: We use smart routing, live KV cache, and continuous batching tuned per workload. For interactive flows we recommend pinning a low-latency variant or Dedicated capacity with a low-concurrency config. There is a tradeoff: lower latency tends to increase per-token cost.
[02:30] [02:45] Dan Cooper: Can your KV cache play well with our multi-tenant prompt templates? We have many patient-profiles reusing prefixes.
[02:52] Ravi Patel: Yes, prefix caching helps a lot for repeated prefixes; the only gotcha is if templates vary per tenant and you can't share cache. We can recommend a per-tenant cache shard strategy in the Dedicated configuration.
[03:07] [03:30] Marta Silva: Security — we need KMS integration and proof of key rotation policy. Legal also asked about the audit logs retention period. Right now we need 12 months retention with export hooks.
[03:45] Sophie Chen: We have KMS integrations with both cloud providers and bring-your-own-key via HSM. Audit logs are configurable; by default we keep 90 days in the console but we can configure longer retention and S3 exports for 12 months. We'll send the exact config options.
[04:05] Tyrell Gomez: Great. Also: SSO. Last time SAMEL setup doc had step that didn't match our IdP. We need a more specific SAML sample for Okta.
[04:14] Sophie Chen: Apologies — the auto doc generator sometimes mislabels. We'll send a trimmed SAML guide specifically for Okta that includes metadata XML and sample assertions.
[04:22] [04:40] Aisha Rahman: On the cost side, our biggest questions: if we move to Dedicated, what's the breakpoint where Dedicated actually saves money? We want a simple decision rule.
[04:53] Ravi Patel: We can model that — typically if sustained token throughput for the main pipeline is more than X tokens per minute for Y% of the hour, Dedicated with optimized quantization (int8) and batching is cheaper. We'll prepare a 'break-even' slide with your sample profiles. Note that int8 quantization can reduce quality slightly; we should run evals.
[05:15] Dan Cooper: Eval threshold — what are acceptable delta metrics? We need a formal SLA for quality drift during quantization.
[05:23] Sophie Chen: We recommend establishing guardrails: rouge/emd style evals for generation or ROC-AUC for classification, plus a user-facing metric like edit distance on output. We'll work with you to pick prompt sets and thresholds.
[05:35] [06:00] Marta Silva: Another infra question: for the perf run we requested a test inside our VPC. Do you support Private deployment or VPC peering for bench runs?
[06:09] Ravi Patel: Yes, we support a Private deployment and we also can run a temporary test cluster in your VPC if networking allows. For a short perf window we commonly do a dedicated instance deployed into a test subnet with peered routes. There are firewall and KMS key considerations though.
[06:28] Aisha Rahman: Ok, we want that test. Can you run the perf with quantized models and with the cache enabled/disabled so we can see the delta?
[06:36] Ravi Patel: Absolutely — we'll run four permutations: hosted non-quantized, hosted quantized, Dedicated non-quantized, Dedicated quantized — each with cache on/off in representative traffic. That will take about 1.5–2 hours.
[06:54] [07:10] Tyrell Gomez: Finance wants a 90-day forecast and a recommended commitment band, and a runbook for throttling during spikes. Can you provide the runbook?
[07:20] Sophie Chen: Yes, we'll share a cost runbook and an operational throttling playbook — steps include: identify offending job, enable autoscale burst or apply route-based throttle, fallback to a cheaper model variant, and escalate to Redwood operations if needed.
[07:36] [07:50] Dan Cooper: Competitors — side question — we evaluated Anthropic and tried Vertex AI too. Anthropic had a cleaner safety envelope but cost was higher on sustained workloads. Keep that in mind as we negotiate.
[08:02] Sophie Chen: Understood. We'll make sure to highlight the cost/latency tradeoffs for your use case.
[08:10] [08:25] *15-minute deep dive on July 12th spike*
[08:27] Marta Silva: The spike was a retry loop triggered by an internal scheduler. Net result was a 4x token count for an hour. Had we had a Dedicated warm pool we would have absorbed it without error but still would have burned tokens.
[08:40] Ravi Patel: Right — Dedicated buys throughput predictability but doesn't stop retries. The runbook and circuit-breaker at the orchestration layer are important.
[08:53] Aisha Rahman: Can Redwood expose per-route token limits we can enforce on our side?
[08:58] Sophie Chen: Yes — per-route quotas exist and can be enforced via the Console or API. Also we can add throttles and alerts to the route.
[09:07] [09:30] *Discussion of pilot success metrics*
[09:33] Sophie Chen: Proposed pilot metrics: 1) 99th percentile latency < 200 ms for clinician flows; 2) cost per 1k interactions reduction of 20% vs current hosted baseline after quantization; 3) quality delta within agreed threshold on eval set. Thoughts?
[09:46] Aisha Rahman: That seems fair. We also want zero PII leakage in logs and CFR for audit.
[09:52] Sophie Chen: We have PII redaction tooling and can configure log scrubbing; we can also do a short log sweep during the perf test.
[09:59] [10:20] Dan Cooper: Timeline — we need to have a commitment decision by end of August to align budget. Does that timeline work?
[10:27] Sophie Chen: Yes — perf run in week of Aug 10, evaluation and back-of-envelope cost model by Aug 14, final recommendation by Aug 20.
[10:36] Tyrell Gomez: Regarding contracts — we need the 30/60 day termination terms for the Dedicated commit, and clarity on burst credits.
[10:43] Lena Ortiz: I'll loop in legal and procurement and send the standard Dedicated term sheet. Burst credits are documented in the plan; we'll surface the exact numbers in the runbook.
[10:56] [11:15] *Technical aside: quantization and quality checks*
[11:18] Ravi Patel: For quantization we'll run int8 and optionally bfloat16 depending on the GPU family. We will run your eval set and provide a per-prompt delta table. Also will show token throughput improvements.
[11:32] Aisha Rahman: One concern: we use structured output heavily and sometimes quantized models hallucinate slot names. Please pay special attention to structured output tests.
[11:42] Ravi Patel: Noted — we'll include structured output checks and function-calling style tests.
[11:50] [12:10] *Wrap and recap*
[12:12] Sophie Chen: Okay quick recap — action items: Redwood sends SOC2 and Okta SAML guide by Aug 3; customer provides sample profiles and prompts by Aug 5; Redwood SE runs perf test week of Aug 10 and delivers break-even slide and cost runbook by Aug 14; finance to confirm budget by Aug 6. Lena will share Dedicated term sheet to procurement.
[12:33] Dan Cooper: Sounds good. Marta and Aisha will prep the prompt sets.
[12:37] Aisha Rahman: We'll also include a 'stress' profile that replicates the retry pattern.
[12:42] Sophie Chen: Great — we'll mark those in the action items. Any final questions?
[12:47] Tyrell Gomez: No, thanks.
[12:49] Sophie Chen: All right thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and post the artifacts in the shared drive.
[12:56] Meeting end.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-typed product names (SAMEL instead of SAML), 'K-V cash' sometimes appears for KV cache, speaker labels may switch to Speaker 1/2 in imported segments.
crm_notes: Customer is on a free evaluation tier for two critical pipelines; usage has ramped 3x over last quarter. Budget decision expected end of August. CSM flagged procurement readiness gap: Tritonix requires 12-month audit log retention and Okta SSO example. Recommend prioritizing the perf-run and security packet to keep momentum.
post_call_feedback: Customer appreciated the concrete runbook approach; main risk is internal orchestration retries which will require changes on their side. They asked to avoid broad claims about quantization quality and to show empirical deltas.
